subject: lavaGolem
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: lava golem of basalt plates and molten seams.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
Looking at the side view, the halo seems a bit too detached from the body with its connecting rod—I'm considering pulling it closer to the head to tighten that composition.

Then there's the proportion issue: the head looks boxy and sunken between oversized pauldrons, so I want to enlarge the eyes and brighten them a bit for more character. The floating ember particles and halo rings read fine as-is, but the torso's lava glow is rendering as a washed-out salmon pink instead of the saturated, intense color I want for that Genshin-style look, so the material needs richer saturation.

I'll darken the LAVA color constant from the flat orange-salmon to a deeper, more intense orange-red, keeping the emissive strength similar so the glow still reads but the base hue stays saturated rather than washed out. Now I'm checking the foot/ankle placement relative to the stage floor height to make sure the legs don't clip or float.

Going through the rest of the figure: hands hang naturally near the stage, the jaw/teeth detail works, the torso-to-pauldron proportions read fine from the side, and the rock pillars with glowing tops plus floating lava spikes look good. The main weakness I'm noting is the face silhouette — the head box is too flat and dark, so I want to add a glowing brow ridge, cheek plates, and chin detailing to give it more readable structure.

I'm also planning to add a glowing mouth interior, a crown flame, bigger eyes, a horn-base glow, and some lava cracks across the forehead for extra character. For Genshin-style flair, I'm considering adding a few floating basalt shards orbiting the golem with ember glow, and possibly a pyro vision-like orb embedded in the chest.

Adding floating rock shards around the halo with glowing seams, then adjusting the pauldron stack so it's less flat and blocky by adding thin glowing strips between tiers. I'm listing out edits: adjusting the lava color, enlarging the eyes, and adding head details like cheek glow slits and forehead cracks, inserting these near the existing emblem lighting calls.

Computing the exact coordinates for the cracks and glow slits—figuring out face positions on the cheeks, forehead, and side blocks so the cracks line up with the front surfaces of each head component.

I'm also planning floating shards around the halo area using scaled basalt dodecahedrons, positioning them at scattered points above and around the head before adding the mouth-opening logic.

I check the halo rod geometry connecting to the bottom of the halo circle, decide the mismatch is minor and leave it as-is, then confirm other details like shoulder spikes and torso emissive values look fine before finalizing the edit, making sure each search string I'm using for replacement is unique in the file.

Adjusting eye size and position so it stays within the face plate bounds, shrinking it slightly to 0.24x0.12 at a shifted x-offset to avoid overlapping the block edge.
